subject: History
description: Causes, programme, Khilafat alliance, Chauri Chaura, withdrawal, significance

questions.stem: The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22) was launched under the leadership of:
questions.explanation: Non-Cooperation Movement (NCM) — Gandhi's first nationwide mass movement. Approved at the special Calcutta session of INC (Sep 1920) and ratified at Nagpur session (Dec 1920). Tilak — passed away on 1 Aug 1920, the very day NCM was launched (also Khilafat Day). Gokhale — Gandhi's political mentor, died 1915. Bose — emerged later, in the 1930s. Programme: surrender titles, boycott of councils, courts, schools, foreign cloth; promote khadi, swadeshi, national education (Jamia Millia Islamia, Kashi Vidyapith, Gujarat Vidyapith founded), Hindu-Muslim unity, removal of untouchability.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Two events that triggered Gandhi's call for the Non-Cooperation Movement were:

options.option_text: Quit India Resolution and Cripps Mission
Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919) and the Khilafat issue (post-Treaty of Sèvres)
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement
Battle of Plassey and Permanent Settlement

questions.explanation: Triggers: (1) Jallianwala Bagh (13 April 1919) under General Dyer at Amritsar — followed by the Hunter Committee report (1920) which Gandhi found unsatisfactory. Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest. (2) Khilafat issue — the Allies' harsh post-WW1 treatment of the Ottoman Caliph (Treaty of Sèvres, 1920) angered Indian Muslims. Khilafat Committee (Ali brothers — Maulana Mohammad Ali + Shaukat Ali) and INC joined hands → Hindu-Muslim unity. (3) The Rowlatt Act (1919) — Gandhi's first satyagraha was against this. The Khilafat issue collapsed in 1924 when Mustafa Kemal Atatürk himself abolished the Caliphate in Turkey.

questions.stem: The Non-Cooperation Movement was abruptly WITHDRAWN by Gandhi in February 1922 after the:

options.option_text: Chauri Chaura incident (5 Feb 1922) — a mob set fire to a police station killing 22 policemen

questions.explanation: Chauri Chaura — Gorakhpur district, UP. On 5 Feb 1922, a peaceful procession of nationalists turned violent after police fired; the agitated crowd set fire to the police station, killing 22 policemen. Gandhi was deeply disturbed by the violence — withdrew the NCM on 12 Feb 1922 (Bardoli Resolution). Many leaders (Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Subhash Bose) opposed the withdrawal — felt it killed momentum at its peak. Gandhi was arrested on 10 March 1922, tried by Justice Broomfield, sentenced to 6 years (the 'Great Trial'). The withdrawal led to the formation of the Swaraj Party (Jan 1923) by C.R. Das + Motilal Nehru — they wanted to enter the councils to wreck them from within.

questions.stem: The Tilak Swaraj Fund — the financial backbone of the Non-Cooperation Movement — collected approximately how much?

options.option_text: ₹1 crore (within six months — a remarkable feat in 1921)

questions.explanation: Tilak Swaraj Fund — set up at the Nagpur session (Dec 1920) in memory of Tilak. Target ₹1 crore in 6 months, attained promptly — symbolised mass financial support for the movement. Used for funding khadi work, national schools, swadeshi industries, propaganda. The Nagpur session also reorganised the Congress — pradesh committees by linguistic states (a forerunner of linguistic states reorganisation later in 1956), Hindi as a major Congress language, lower membership fee to mass-enrol peasants/workers. Membership rose from ~60,000 to ~20 lakh.

questions.stem: Which leader famously renounced his British KNIGHTHOOD in protest after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, foreshadowing the Non-Cooperation spirit?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore — renounced his Knighthood (Sir, conferred 1915) on 31 May 1919 in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, in a letter to Viceroy Chelmsford ('the time has come when badges of honour make our shame glaring in their incongruous context of humiliation'). Gandhi later returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal (1920) when launching NCM. Tagore — Nobel Literature 1913 (first non-European Nobel laureate); composed Jana Gana Mana (India) and Amar Shonar Bangla (Bangladesh); founded Visva-Bharati at Santiniketan. Lala Lajpat Rai — 'Sher-e-Punjab', injured in lathi-charge at Lahore against Simon Commission (1928), died shortly thereafter.

questions.stem: Of the following national universities/educational institutions founded during the Non-Cooperation Movement era, which one was established in DELHI?

options.option_text: Jamia Millia Islamia (founded 1920 at Aligarh, shifted to Delhi in 1925)

questions.explanation: Jamia Millia Islamia ('national Muslim university') — founded 22 Oct 1920 at Aligarh by Mohammad Ali Jauhar, Hakim Ajmal Khan, Dr Mukhtar Ahmad Ansari, Dr Zakir Husain (later President of India 1967-69), and Maulana Mahmud Hasan, in response to the Non-Cooperation call to boycott colonial education. Shifted to Karol Bagh, Delhi (1925), then Okhla, New Delhi (1935); central university status 1988. Other NCM-era national institutions — Kashi Vidyapith (Varanasi, 1921, Bhagwan Das), Gujarat Vidyapith (Ahmedabad, 1920, Gandhi himself), Bihar Vidyapith (1921), Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (Pune, 1921). Visva-Bharati was founded earlier by Tagore in 1921, but its philosophical roots go back to 1901 Santiniketan ashram.

questions.stem: Which Tribal / Peasant uprising in the Madras Presidency (1922-24), led by Alluri Sitarama Raju, took inspiration from the Non-Cooperation Movement but eventually turned to armed methods?
questions.explanation: Rampa Rebellion (1922-24) — led by Alluri Sitarama Raju ('Manyam Veerudu' — hero of the jungle) in the Visakhapatnam-Godavari agency tracts of Madras Presidency. Tribal grievances: forest laws restricting podu (shifting cultivation), forced labour. Initially inspired by Gandhi's NCM but turned to armed raids on police stations after NCM's withdrawal. Alluri was captured and shot on 7 May 1924. The Mappila Rebellion (Malabar, 1921) — coincided with NCM in Kerala; began as Khilafat-inspired but turned communal. Tana Bhagat (Jharkhand, Oraon tribals, Jatra Bhagat) — also drew on NCM ideas. These uprisings showed the deeper rural reach of nationalist politics during 1920-22.
